newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver fall on weak world trend.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver fall on weak world trend.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat ended 90 rupees lower at 4,805 rupees per 10 grammes on continued selling pressure following weak world trend.
** Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 grammes each) closed 1,100 rupees lower at 56,200 rupees per piece.
** Silver (.999) closed 55 rupees lower at 7,500 rupees per kg against the previous closing of 7,555 rupees following a fresh setback in the world market.
TODAY'S CLOSING (BOMBAY) PVS CLOSING
Gold 24 carat 4,805 rupees per 10 gms (-90) 4,895
Silver.999 7,500 rupees per kg (-55) 7,555
Gold 24 carat closed 90 rupees lower at 4,805 rupees per 10 grammes on selling pressure from stockists following a setback in the world market, dealers said.
Gold was down 55 rupees per 10 grammes on Wednesday.
Gold prices in the world market shed recent gains on reports that a large European bank was planning to sell gold, said M.L. Damani, president of the Bombay Bullion Association.
"This triggered selling in the local market," he said.
Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 grammes each) closed 1,100 rupees lower at 56,200 rupees. They were down 700 rupees on Wednesday.
"I am excepting gold prices to attract fresh seasonal buying at reduced levels next week," Damani said.
Silver (.999) was down 55 rupees at 7,500 rupees per kg.
"Silver prices opened lower following overnight losses in the world market but moved in a narrow band on limited arrivals during the day," one broker said.
Silver was down 95 rupees per kg on Wednesday.
The Bombay bullion market will remain closed on Friday for a Hindu festival, dealers said.
(Conversion $=35.86 rupees)
-- Bombay Commodities +91-22 265 9000
